title: Real Estate Brokerage Scope Tasks: Nightly vs. Periodic Duty Roster for Brokerage Offices
seoTitle: Real Estate Brokerage Scope Tasks: Nightly vs. Periodic Duty Roster
metaDescription: Real estate brokerage scope tasks split into nightly, weekly and monthly duties with labor minutes per zone. See what drives extra hours, then compare quotes.
excerpt: A brokerage office needs a duty roster built around its bullpen, closing rooms, and walk-in traffic rather than a generic office checklist. This roster separates nightly tasks from periodic ones and explains which specialty items raise labor hours.
quickAnswer: A real estate brokerage scope should assign nightly duties to restrooms, the breakroom, entry matting, closing rooms, and bullpen trash, while vacuuming desks, glass, and detail dusting rotate weekly. Periodic work such as carpet extraction, LVT scrubbing, and high dusting is scheduled monthly or quarterly. Hoteling-desk disinfection, post-event breakroom resets, and storefront glass are the specialty tasks that push brokerage labor above the standard 3,500 sq ft per hour office pace.

blocks.text: Building the Roster Around How Brokerages Actually Use Space

A brokerage office does not get dirty evenly. Agents cluster in the bullpen around Monday sales meetings, closing rooms fill on offer-review days, and the breakroom hosts catered lunches for training sessions and lender presentations. Weekend open-house prep sends agents in and out on Saturday mornings. A useful scope converts those patterns into a duty roster: tasks that must happen every service night, tasks that rotate through the week, and periodic projects scheduled on a calendar.

Start by labeling six zones on the floor plan: entry and reception, bullpen and hoteling desks, closing and conference rooms, broker and manager offices, transaction coordinator and file area, and restrooms with the breakroom. Each zone gets its own nightly and periodic tasks. This format makes it easy to see where a vendor is putting labor and where it is cutting corners.

blocks.caption: Nightly tasks for a 3,200 sq ft brokerage storefront serviced twice weekly
rows: Vacuum walk-off mats, dust-mop and damp-mop entry LVT, spot-clean door glass and push bar
Empty deskside bins and recycling, wipe cleared hoteling desk surfaces, spot vacuum
All bins emptied, shared desks wiped
Wipe tables, chair arms, pens tray and conference phone; vacuum; spot-clean glass
Disinfect fixtures and touch points, restock, polish mirrors, mop
Wipe counters and tables, clean sink, microwave, fridge handles, coffee station; mop floor
Disinfect door handles, light switches, copier and printer panels, lockbox key cabinet exterior

blocks.text: Those tasks total roughly 80 minutes per service night for a 3,200 sq ft office. At the ISSA pace of 3,500 sq ft per hour, a generic office the same size would need about 55 minutes. The 25-minute gap comes from bullpen trash volume, hoteling desk wiping, and closing room detail, and it explains why brokerage bids often land in the upper half of the $0.09-$0.15 per sq ft benchmark range.

items: Full vacuum of the bullpen including under desks and along cable runs, alternating halves on each service night.
Clean interior glass on closing rooms and the broker's office, both faces and full height.
Damp-dust monitor arms, desk partitions, filing cabinet tops, and window sills without moving agent paperwork.
Wipe breakroom cabinet fronts, appliance exteriors, and the inside of the microwave and refrigerator door gaskets.
Vacuum upholstered reception seating and closing room chairs.
Descale restroom faucets, clean partition walls, and wipe baseboards.
Clean the inside face of storefront windows and listing display frames.

blocks.text: Periodic tasks protect floors and air quality and are the line items most often left out of low bids. Monthly duties include high dusting of light fixtures, vents, and the tops of tall cabinets; spot extraction of carpet tile stains in the bullpen; and a deep clean of the breakroom refrigerator if the brokerage permits it. Quarterly duties include hot-water extraction of bullpen carpet tile, scrubbing LVT or VCT in the entry and breakroom, and cleaning return-air grilles.

Our benchmark amortizes quarterly floor programs at $0.03-$0.06 per sq ft per month. For 3,200 sq ft that is $96-$192 per month; for a 7,500 sq ft flagship it is $225-$450. Listing it separately keeps nightly labor from being quietly reduced to fund a weekend extraction.

blocks.title: Equipment that speeds the nightly floor pass
blocks.text: In storefront brokerages with LVT or VCT, a Rubbermaid Commercial 36-Inch Cotton Dust Mop with a 60-inch handle and 360-degree swivel head clears entry grit across wide aisles in a few passes. Where reception or the broker's office has wood floors, the Bona Commercial System Multi-Surface Hardwood Mop Kit pairs an 18-inch aluminum base and telescoping handle with washable microfiber dusting and wet pads that are wood safe. In closing rooms, a Medify MA-50 H13 True HEPA purifier rated for about 1,100 sq ft with four fan speeds and a quiet 36 dBA minimum setting helps control dust between visits.

blocks.text: Turning the Roster Into Contract Language

items.name: Attach the zone map and roster
items.text: Include both as exhibits to the RFP so every bidder prices identical nightly, weekly, and periodic duties.

items.name: Define desk rules
items.text: State that crews wipe only cleared hoteling desks and never move agent files, keys, or signed documents.

items.name: Set service nights to match the calendar
items.text: Schedule service after the Monday sales meeting and before the weekend so labor follows actual soil load.

items.name: Price periodic work separately
items.text: Request a 12-month periodic calendar with costs for extraction, floor scrubbing, and high dusting.

items.name: Inspect monthly
items.text: Walk the zones with the vendor supervisor each month and score against the roster standards.

faqs.q: How many hours does it take to clean a 3,200 sq ft real estate office?
faqs.a: Plan on 75-90 minutes per service night once bullpen trash, hoteling desks, two restrooms, and the breakroom are included. That is longer than the roughly 55 minutes the ISSA 3,500 sq ft per hour pace implies for a generic office of the same size.

Only shared hoteling desks that agents have cleared. Assigned desks with papers, keys, or files should be left alone except for emptying the bin. Put this rule in writing so the vendor is protected and transaction files stay secure.

faqs.q: What products should be used on shared desks and closing room tables?
faqs.a: Use an EPA-registered disinfectant on high-touch points and shared desks, following the label dwell time, and a Green Seal or Safer Choice general cleaner for routine surfaces. The vendor must keep Safety Data Sheets on site under OSHA HazCom, 29 CFR 1910.1200.

faqs.q: How often should bullpen carpet be extracted?
faqs.a: Quarterly for busy bullpens with rolling chairs and food at desks, or twice a year for quieter offices. Spot extraction monthly prevents stains from setting between full extractions.

faqs.q: Is weekend cleaning worth it for a brokerage?
faqs.a: If agents use the office heavily on Saturdays, a short Saturday evening visit for restrooms and trash is cheaper than adding a full weekday visit. Expect specialty hourly rates of $55-$95 with a one- or two-hour minimum.
